content_voiceover: This is a dense but high yield reference table on causes of macrocytosis, defined as MCV over ninety seven, with a column showing likelihood of MCV over one hundred ten for each cause. The highest yield causes with high likelihood of a very elevated MCV are cobalamin or folate deficiency, cytotoxic or immunosuppressive drugs, antiviral drugs, aplastic anemia or pure red cell aplasia, and as a lab artifact, cold agglutinins or severe hyperglycemia falsely elevating the measured MCV. Moderate likelihood causes include alcohol with or without liver disease, myelodysplastic syndrome, copper deficiency anemia, reticulocytosis from hemolytic anemia, and non-alcoholic liver disease. Low likelihood causes include anticonvulsants, myeloproliferative disease or leukemia, sideroblastic anemia, hypothyroidism, pregnancy, chronic lung disease or smoking, and multiple myeloma. The key testable pattern for boards, when you see a truly massive MCV, well above one hundred ten, your differential should narrow sharply toward B12 or folate deficiency, myelosuppressive or antiviral drug effects, aplastic anemia, or a spurious lab artifact like cold agglutinins or hyperglycemia, rather than the more common but milder causes like alcohol or hypothyroidism.
keypoints: MCV >110 fL → think B12/folate deficiency, cytotoxic/antiviral drugs, aplastic anemia
Cold agglutinins & severe hyperglycemia = artifactual (spurious) macrocytosis
Moderate causes: alcohol, MDS, copper deficiency, reticulocytosis, liver disease
Low likelihood: hypothyroidism, pregnancy, smoking, myeloma
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, remember that a very high MCV, well above one hundred ten, points to a short list of high likelihood causes, cobalamin or folate deficiency, cytotoxic or antiviral drugs, and aplastic anemia or pure red cell aplasia. Also remember the artifact category, cold agglutinins and severe hyperglycemia can spuriously elevate the measured MCV without true macrocytosis. Milder or more moderate elevations are more often from alcohol, liver disease, myelodysplastic syndrome, or ongoing reticulocytosis from hemolysis.
